false_assumption.statement: Alicia Driscoll was the thief who repeatedly stole and returned jewels.
false_assumption.why_it_seems_reasonable: Alicia was the most conspicuous member of the group and had been associated with several thefts, making her the obvious suspect. The pattern of stolen items coinciding with her presence reinforced this belief.
false_assumption.what_it_hides: The true culprit was Caroline West, who used Alicia's identity and slippers to mislead others and conceal her own guilt.

mechanism_description: Caroline West disguised herself by wearing Alicia Driscoll's slippers to access Violet Strange's room via the balcony. She took the pendant by reaching through the open window and stole it, believing it would expose Alicia's misdeeds. The red-stained paste on the pendant marked her fingers, revealing her guilt despite her attempt to conceal it with gloves.

discriminating_test.design: Violet Strange applied a red-stained paste to her pendant, which would mark the fingers of anyone who touched it. During the investigation, all suspects were asked to remove gloves and show their hands. The presence or absence of red stains on their fingers served as a concrete test of who had handled the pendant.
discriminating_test.knowledge_revealed: This test revealed that Caroline West's fingers were stained despite her attempts to conceal them with gloves, proving her guilt.
discriminating_test.pass_condition: The true thief must have red-stained fingers matching the paste on the pendant, eliminating all others.
